exec: Seoul Shinmun reports that ransomware-hit organisations in South Korea rose 175% and 46 of the top 100 listed companies got a high-risk D or F rating.
geo_basis: country as stated by the source
org: Zscaler / SecurityScorecard (as reported by Seoul Shinmun)
plain: A Korean newspaper reports that the number of ransomware-hit organisations in South Korea rose 175% in a year while falling 3% worldwide, and that 46 of the top 100 listed companies were rated high security risk.

key_findings: Seoul Shinmun says Zscaler's 2026 ransomware report shows the number of ransomware-hit organisations in South Korea rose 175% from April of last year to March of this year versus the year before, while the worldwide figure fell 3%.

Seoul Shinmun says SecurityScorecard rated 46 of South Korea's top 100 listed companies by market capitalisation in the high-risk D or F grades, and that 94 were linked to external partners with a breach history.

summary: Seoul Shinmun reports that, according to Zscaler's 2026 ransomware report, the number of ransomware-hit organisations in South Korea rose 175% from April of last year to March of this year compared with the year before, while the worldwide figure fell 3%. It also reports that SecurityScorecard rated 46 of the top 100 listed companies in the high-risk D or F grades.
title: Seoul Shinmun: Zscaler report says South Korean ransomware victims rose 175%; SecurityScorecard rates 46 of top 100 firms high risk

validation.note: Single publisher, Seoul Shinmun; it relays Zscaler and SecurityScorecard findings, the original reports were not read.
